title: People Ops — Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Guide
author: Ava Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose: This guide documents Redwood Inference's standard practices for hiring, new-employee onboarding, performance and feedback cycles, and the manager responsibilities needed to run these processes consistently. It is intended for hiring managers, people-ops partners, recruiters, hiring panel members, and new-manager cohorts.

Scope: Applies to full-time employees, contractors with multi-month engagements, and managers of those hires. Exceptions (e.g., executive hires, localized employment law needs) are handled with People Ops and Legal.

---

1) Hiring process (end-to-end)

Intro: Our hiring process balances speed and quality while ensuring a fair candidate experience and defensible decisioning. The workflow below is the canonical flow for most roles.

Key roles and responsibilities:
- Hiring Manager: defines role requirements, approves interviewers, leads final hiring decision.
- Recruiter: sources candidates, schedules interviews, manages offer pipeline.
- People Ops Partner: approves comp band, processes offers, runs background checks, and supports relocation/work-eligibility.
- Interview Panel: completes scorecards and provides calibrated feedback.

Canonical steps (timeline expectation in parentheses):
1. Requisition creation and approval (1-3 business days)
   - Hiring manager fills the requisition template in Workday/Grove with role description, team impact, must-have vs nice-to-have qualifications, and target level.
   - People Ops approves headcount and initial comp band.
2. Sourcing & screening (1-3 weeks depending on role)
   - Recruiter sources and runs a 15-30 minute phone screen to confirm basic fit and eligibility.
3. Interview loop (1-2 weeks)
   - Typical loop: technical/problem-solving session, role-specific deep dive, collaboration/peer interview, and a manager interview.
   - Each interviewer completes the standard interview scorecard within 48 hours.
4. Calibration & decision (2-4 business days)
   - Hiring manager reviews scorecards and holds a short calibration meeting with panel if feedback diverges. People Ops must be included if there are compensation exceptions.
5. Offer & approvals (1-3 business days)
   - Hiring manager provides recommended band and level. People Ops confirms comp band and prepares offer packet. Legal signs off on special terms.
6. Background checks & acceptance (3-7 business days)
   - Offer is subject to background verification (when required) and signed offer letter.
7. Start date & preboarding (2-4 weeks prior to start)
   - Recruiter shares welcome packet, first-week agenda, and IT logistics.

Interview scorecard (required fields):
- Role: (string)
- Interviewer: (string)
- Date: (YYYY-MM-DD)
- Core competencies assessed (bulleted list)
- Rating (1-5) for each competency
- Summary of strengths and risks
- Hiring recommendation: Strong hire | Hire | Neutral | No hire

Offer approval thresholds (table):
- < $10k above midpoint: People Ops approval
- $10k–$30k above midpoint: People Ops + Hiring Director approval
- > $30k above midpoint: VP People Ops + Finance approval

Diversity, equity & inclusion checkpoints:
- Use inclusive job descriptions (People Ops template).
- Interview panels should include at least one cross-functional interviewer for senior roles when possible.
- Track demographic metrics per requisition in the hiring dashboard.

---

2) Preboarding & Employee Onboarding (0-90 days)

Principles: New hires should feel welcomed, productive, and connected. Onboarding is a shared responsibility between People Ops, the hiring manager, and the new hire's team.

Preboarding (2-14 days before start):
- Send welcome email with first-day logistics, parking/transit info, remote-kit shipping (if remote), and links to required paperwork.
- Create accounts: SSO, email, Slack, Okta, and GitHub (or role-specific tools). IT ticket created and tracked by the hiring manager in the onboarding tracker.

Day 0-7 (Week 1): First-week goals
- Day 0: Welcome & HR orientation (People Ops) covering benefits, security training, and company values.
- Days 1-2: Team introductions, role overview, and set up dev environment/access.
- Days 3-5: Shadowing sessions, first small deliverable, and sync to set 30/60/90 expectations.

30/60/90 day plan (manager & new hire collaborate; sample structure):
- 30-day goals: Understand codebase and key services, complete first small ticket or documentation update, meet cross-functional partners.
- 60-day goals: Own larger tasks, ship a bugfix or feature, and take ownership of a recurring operational task.
- 90-day goals: Lead an initiative, present a retrospective of onboarding, and receive formal 90-day check-in from manager & People Ops.

Onboarding checklist (mandatory items):
- Signed offer & completed I-9 or local-equivalent forms
- Benefits enrollment completed within 30 days
- Security & compliance training completed within first week
- Manager assigns mentor/buddy
- First performance goal entered into performance system

Tools and trackers:
- Onboarding tracker (People Ops maintained) — includes tasks assigned to IT, Manager, and Employee.
- New hire survey at day 7 and day 30 to capture issues and improve the program.

Remote onboarding specifics:
- Schedule overlapping hours for first two weeks with timezone-aware meeting bundles.
- Ship hardware before start date when allowed by local policy.
- Set explicit communication norms (Slack channels, async expectations).

---

3) Performance & feedback cycles

Cadence and intent: Redwood uses a continuous feedback model complemented by structured cycles to calibrate performance and development. The primary cycles are:
- Weekly 1:1s (manager-directed)
- Quarterly objectives & check-ins
- Annual performance review (calibration + compensation decisions)

Manager responsibilities (ongoing):
- Hold weekly 1:1s with direct reports and document notes/action items.
- Provide actionable feedback (both praise and development).
- Maintain performance notes in the performance system for recurrent patterns or significant achievements.
- Support career conversations and outline development path.

Quarterly cycle (example timeline):
1. Goal setting (week 1 of quarter): Managers and employees agree on 3-5 measurable OKRs or success criteria.
2. Mid-quarter check-in (week 6): Informal review of progress, blockers, and resource needs.
3. End-of-quarter review (final two weeks): Employee self-assessment, manager assessment, calibration by Director.

Annual review & calibration:
- Timeline: Reviews open in November; calibration and comp decisions in December; compensation notices delivered in January.
- Calibration panels are organized by People Ops and include cross-team Directors to ensure equitable leveling and pay practices.

Feedback best practices (for managers):
- Be specific: cite examples and impact.
- Make it timely: give feedback as close to the event as practical.
- Balance: aim for a 3:1 ratio of constructive feedback to praise over time.
- Document: capture feedback in the performance system to support calibration.

Low-performance & performance improvement plans (PIP):
- Trigger: consistent missing of agreed goals despite coaching (documented).
- Process: Manager notifies People Ops; People Ops reviews case, recommends timeframe (typically 60-90 days), and provides PIP template and coaching resources.
- Outcomes: PIP successfully completed leads to resumed normal cadence; unsuccessful PIP leads to further HR actions per local employment law.

---

4) Manager playbook (day-to-day operational checklist)

First 30 days for new managers:
- Complete Manager Accelerator training (People Ops L&D).
- Run 1:1s weekly and set team norms.
- Review direct reports' 30/60/90 plans and open roles.
- Schedule skip-level meetings with reports' peers and managers for context.

Recruiting-specific manager checklist:
- Write inclusive job descriptions using People Ops template.
- Approve interview panel and ensure panel diversity when possible.
- Review scorecards within 48 hours and provide final recommendation.
- Work with People Ops on ramp plan and first deliverables.

Comp & promotion guidelines (high level):
- Promotions require manager recommendation, peer manager calibration, and People Ops approval.
- Compensation adjustments outside band follow the approval thresholds outlined in the Hiring section.

Manager escalation matrix (who to contact for common issues):
- Offer or comp questions: People Ops Partner
- Employment law or contract exceptions: Legal
- Benefits and payroll issues: HR Operations
- Performance process and PIP: People Ops + HR Operations

---

5) Templates and artifacts (links provided in the company wiki)

Included templates (examples):
- Job requisition template
- Interview scorecard (standardized fields)
- Offer letter templates by region
- 30/60/90 plan template
- PIP template and coaching checklist
- New manager onboarding checklist

Sample interview email snippet (for recruiters):
"Hi [Candidate],
Thank you for applying to Redwood Inference. We'd like to invite you to a [30/60]-minute interview with [Interviewer Name] on [Date]. Please let us know if the time works or suggest alternatives. You'll receive a calendar invite with a short prep note and the role's job spec."

---

6) Metrics and continuous improvement

People Ops monitors the following leading metrics: time-to-fill, offer-accept rate, new-hire retention at 90 days, hiring diversity metrics, and new-hire satisfaction (Day 7 and Day 30). Quarterly People Ops retros review these metrics and propose changes to the process.

Document ownership and review cycle:
- Owner: People Ops (Ava Chen)
- Review cadence: Annual review or sooner if policy or legal changes occur.
- How to propose changes: Open a PR in the People Ops handbook repo or email people-ops@redwood.ai with a suggested update and rationale.

Appendix: Common FAQs
Q: What if a hiring manager wants to skip interview stages to move faster?
A: Only approved by Director+ and People Ops; panel members must still complete scorecards and People Ops will audit the hire.

Q: Are contractors onboarded the same way?
A: Yes for access and security training; some benefits and paperwork vary — consult People Ops.

Q: Who sets comp bands?
A: People Ops sets bands in collaboration with Finance and Market comp data; managers recommend a level within that band.

Contact: people-ops@redwood.ai for questions or process exceptions.
